summary.text: 看 is traditionally explained as 手 above 目: a hand shading the eyes to gaze into the distance. The received analysis is not confirmed by a securely dated early inscription.

formation.text: A semantic compound in the received Shuowen analysis: 手 and 目 combine as a hand shading the eyes while gazing. The interpretation is traditional; no securely dated early form here independently confirms the scene.

components.text: 手 is the hand placed above 目 in the traditional gaze-shading interpretation. No distinct earlier form for this graph is established here.
目 is the eye placed below 手 in the traditional interpretation. No distinct earlier form for this graph is established here.

history.text: The received Shuowen account analyzes 看 as 手 above 目 and records the alternate graph 𥉏 with 倝 as a phonetic. The alternate’s date and graphic relationship to 看 are unresolved; the available account does not establish the graph’s development or a corruption between the forms.

uncertainties.text: The traditional hand-shading interpretation is not confirmed by a securely dated early inscription. The earliest written attestation of 看 and the date of 𥉏 remain unresolved.

senses.gloss: gaze or look into the distance
senses.text: The received Shuowen gloss 睎也 is explained in later commentary as shading the eyes with the hand to gaze. This is the earliest sense supported by the cited account, but the earliest historical occurrence of the spoken word is unresolved.
Looking, seeing, and observing are recorded meanings. Their relationship to the gaze gloss and to one another is not dated here.
